A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RCDB and RCDB-S research. The complete main text, algorithms, equations, table, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Appendix E reports original synthetic bandit simulations, including comparisons under four adversarial attacks and varying corruption budgets, averaged over 10 random runs.

after.justification: Appendix E retains the original simulation studies and additionally plots RCDB-S results under the four attacks in Figure 1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same weighted MLE, covariance matrices, weight definitions, and action-selection procedures. RCDB-S already exists in v2; its added experimental curves do not introduce a method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic sigmoid-preference task, five-dimensional features, 32 actions, four attack scenarios, and corruption-budget sweep. Evaluating RCDB-S does not expand data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 1 adds the existing RCDB-S variant to the comparison involving RCDB, MaxInP, CoLSTIM, and MaxPairUCB. The external baseline set and Figure 2 participants remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported protocol remains unchanged: parameter norm 2, T = 2000, cumulative regret, C = ceil(sqrt(T)) in Figure 1, and C = 20, 40, ..., 200 in Figure 2. Revised curves do not establish an undocumented setting change.

E4.justification: Figure 1 extends the existing attack-robustness tests to RCDB-S, providing evidence about its behavior under greedy, random, adversarial, and misleading attacks. The corruption-budget sensitivity study in Figure 2 is unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 random runs and display shaded bands in Figure 1. Neither adds a definition of those bands, seed information, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The principal performance comparison is substantively revised: Figure 1 adds four RCDB-S curves and changes several baseline outcomes substantially. For example, MaxInP's final greedy-attack regret rises from approximately 1,900 to 3,500 under the same reported setup. RCDB-S performs close to RCDB, with slightly higher regret under Adversarial Attack. Figure 2 is unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects the zero-valued branch of the link function in (A.3) from x < 0 to x < -1/2, removing overlapping cases. Equation (A.6) changes the Pinsker factor from sqrt(KL) to sqrt(KL/2). The theorem statements and remaining proof framework are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about robust contextual dueling bandits, nearly optimal regret, unknown corruption budgets, and RCDB-S's improved leading-term dependence. Removing adjectives describing experimental breadth does not change these claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds computational efficiency through avoiding MLE recomputation every round as a future direction. Appendix D newly explains why the fixed-design confidence bounds discussed for Jun et al. (2021) do not directly cover adaptive action selection. Existing experimental interpretations and nonlinear-reward limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation and reproducibility disclosures remain unchanged, including synthetic data generation and experimental budgets. The added RCDB-S curves receive no corresponding new tuning, implementation, hardware, runtime, or code-access details.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jun et al. (2017, 2021), Zhang and Sugiyama (2024), and Sawarni et al. (2024). It also explicitly credits Abeille et al. (2021) for the integral-based argument and clarifies that the previously studied pair-selection rule is not the central contribution. These are localized positioning refinements.

P1.justification: The section and appendix sequence is retained. Local edits add explanations of the lower-bound construction, revise attribution and cross-references, move the strong-adversary footnote into the text, and add acknowledgements; most prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 converts the main text and references to two columns, changes typography and running headers, and extensively reflows algorithm boxes and appendix pages. Figure 1 is redrawn with RCDB-S legend entries and curves, plus expanded vertical scales in the weak-attack panels.

improvement.justification: The local mathematical corrections in (A.3) and (A.6), clearer explanations and attribution, and added empirical evidence for RCDB-S modestly improve precision and support. The benefit is limited by unchanged experimental documentation: Figure 1's caption and discussion still omit RCDB-S and do not explain the revised baseline curves.
